subproblem.title: Divergence commutes with convolution by a locally integrable kernel
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and E = ℝⁿ with Lebesgue measure. Let κ : E → ℝ be locally integrable and g : E → E a C¹ vector field with compact support. Then for every x ∈ E, div(κ * g)(x) = (κ * div g)(x). Here κ * g = convolution κ g (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, i.e. (κ * g)(x) = ∫ κ(t) g(x − t) dt; κ * div g is the scalar convolution; and div = Chapter02.euclideanDivergence, the trace of the Fréchet derivative.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (κ : Rn n → ℝ) (g : Rn n → Rn n), LocallyIntegrable κ volume → ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → ∀ x, Chapter02.euclideanDivergence (convolution κ g (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) x = convolution κ (Chapter02.euclideanDivergence g) (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 1(b) (divergence commutes with convolution), for a general locally integrable kernel κ in place of ρ̌.

Notation. E := ℝⁿ and μ := volume, an additive Haar measure. κ * g := convolution κ g (lsmul ℝ ℝ) μ, so (κ * g)(x) = ∫ κ(t) • g(x − t) dt (E-valued); for scalar φ, κ * φ is defined in the same way. div φ := Chapter02.euclideanDivergence φ, so div φ(x) = trace(fderiv ℝ φ x).

1. Dg := fderiv ℝ g is continuous, since g is C¹ (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). It has compact support, because tsupport Dg ⊆ tsupport g (HasCompactSupport.fderiv).
2. Derivative of the convolution. Apply HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right (g C¹ with compact support, κ locally integrable, μ Haar). For every x ∈ E, κ * g has Fréchet derivative D(κ * g)(x) = ∫ L'(κ(t))(Dg(x − t)) dt, with L' := (lsmul ℝ ℝ).precompR E. Here L'(a)(A) = (lsmul ℝ ℝ a) ∘L A = a • A for a ∈ ℝ and A ∈ E →L[ℝ] E (precompR_apply, compL). Hence fderiv ℝ (κ * g) x = ∫ κ(t) • Dg(x − t) dt.
3. Integrability. The integrand t ↦ κ(t) • Dg(x − t) is Bochner integrable. It is the convolution integrand of κ and Dg at x, and that convolution exists because Dg is continuous with compact support and κ is locally integrable (HasCompactSupport.convolutionExists_right). Concretely, it vanishes outside the compact set x − tsupport g, where κ is integrable and Dg is bounded.
4. Trace through the integral. Let T(A) := trace(A), the LinearMap.trace ℝ E of the underlying linear map of A ∈ E →L[ℝ] E. T is linear on the finite-dimensional space E →L[ℝ] E, hence a continuous linear map (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap applied to trace ∘ coeLM). By ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm and step 3: T(∫ κ(t) • Dg(x − t) dt) = ∫ T(κ(t) • Dg(x − t)) dt.
5. For each t, (lsmul ℝ ℝ (κ t)) ∘L Dg(x − t) = κ(t) • Dg(x − t). So T(κ(t) • Dg(x − t)) = κ(t) · trace(Dg(x − t)) = κ(t) · div g(x − t), by linearity of the trace and the definition of euclideanDivergence.
6. Hence div(κ * g)(x) = T(fderiv ℝ (κ * g) x) = ∫ κ(t) · div g(x − t) dt. This equals convolution κ (Chapter02.euclideanDivergence g) (lsmul ℝ ℝ) μ x, as claimed. ∎
proof_key_steps: Dg = fderiv ℝ g is continuous with compact support.
HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right: D(κ*g)(x) = ∫ κ(t)•Dg(x−t) dt, and the integrand is integrable (convolutionExists_right).
The trace is a continuous linear map on the finite-dimensional space E →L E; integral_comp_comm moves it inside the integral.
trace(κ(t)•Dg(x−t)) = κ(t)·div g(x−t), so div(κ*g)(x) = (κ*div g)(x).

audit.reason: The vector and scalar convolutions elaborate with the intended scalar multiplication. C¹ regularity and compact support make Dg continuous and compactly supported. The convolution derivative formula, integrability and continuous linear trace prove the exact pointwise divergence identity.
